title: Safe duplication and traffic fanout pipeline for model evaluation
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Problem: We need a robust 'fanout' pipeline that safely duplicates production requests for model evaluation (shadow/parallel runs) without risking customer latency, tenant data leakage, or runaway cost. Existing mirroring work focuses on sampling and basic isolation; this ticket designs and implements a production-ready fanout with per-tenant budget gates, KV-cache isolation, and explicit dry-run tracing so we can validate model changes at scale.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Requests can be duplicated to one or more evaluation backends with <=1% added tail latency to production p95 under typical load.
2) Sampling policies support static, stratified, and adaptive (cost-aware) modes and are configurable per-route and per-tenant.
3) Per-tenant budget gates prevent more than X% extra token spend (configurable) and automatically throttle shadow traffic when savings thresholds are hit.
4) Shadow runs are tagged with dry-run telemetry and never write to downstream stateful systems (no external side effects).
5) End-to-end observability: per-route shadow ratio, extra tokens consumed, modeled cost, and discrepancy metrics between prod and shadow outputs are visible in Console.
6) Rollback behavior: when discrepancy or error rate exceeds configured SLO, shadow pipeline must surface signals to auto-rollback/abort experiments and notify on-call.
7) Integration tests and load tests demonstrate stable behavior with 10k rps production baseline and 100% duplication in a staging cluster.
8) Security review completed for telemetry and KMS usage; no PII leaves the VPC in any shadow path.
design_summary: We will implement a fanout service that sits in the routing layer. Core components: 1) Fanout Router — duplicates requests to evaluation workers while propagating original request context and a dry-run header; 2) Sampler — policy engine supporting static, stratified (by tenant/route/region), and adaptive cost-aware sampling using recent token-cost estimates; 3) Isolation Worker Pool — evaluation workers run in separate namespaces with KV cache bypass and reduced resource priority to avoid contention; 4) Budget Gate — per-tenant token budget counter with soft/hard thresholds and automatic shedding; 5) Telemetry & Comparator — sidecar that computes semantic divergence metrics and surfaces alerts. Trade-offs: we prioritize isolation and cost controls over perfect fidelity of runtime environment (some microsecond drift expected due to cache bypass). We avoid writing to external services in shadow runs — use mocks and a sandbox layer for downstream interactions.
non_goals: Replace canary rollouts or A/B routing — this ticket focuses on safe duplication only.
Full-fidelity stateful side-effect replay — we will not attempt to replicate write-side effects to production systems.
On-the-fly model parameter tuning — evaluation runs are read-only for model scoring and telemetry generation.
implementation_notes: Fanout Router will use existing routing hooks in serving runtime; add a new header X-RW-DryRun and context id to link prod vs shadow traces.
Develop a lightweight policy DSL for sampling (percentage, per-tenant cap, stratification keys).
Isolation: evaluation workers should set RW_EVAL=true and use a separate KV namespace; include a runtime flag to optionally reuse cache in non-critical experiments.
Budget Gate uses Redis counters backed by a recovery-safe ledger; failures default to conservative blocking to avoid overspend.
Comparator will ship an initial set of divergence detectors (token-level edit distance, embedding cosine delta, hallucination heuristics) and record signals to Logs and Console metrics.
security_and_privacy_notes: All shadow requests carry an explicit dry-run header and must not trigger side-effects. Telemetry is stripped of any free-text user content before leaving the VPC; detailed payloads are stored only in an encrypted staging bucket with KMS keys managed by Redwood. Security review requested; next steps include confirming KMS access lists and logging retention for compliance.
